lanka_shankari.name: Shankari / Koneswaram
lanka_shankari.architecture: The present headland precinct follows aerial and ground photographs, with the red entrance stair, seated Shiva, wide temple hall and eastern lower Ravana ledge.
lanka_shankari.deity_form: Shankari sacred form remains unresolved. The current temple worships Shiva as Koneswarar and his consort Mathumai Amman.
lanka_shankari.deity_notes: The Shankari guide point records the tradition. The current temple guide separately names Koneswarar, Mathumai Amman, Vinayagar and Murugan.
lanka_shankari.uncertainties: Modern interior bays and cliff elevation are approximate. A measured survey is required for installed deity locations, recovered sculpture and surviving epigraphy.

kanchipuram_kamakshi.name: Kamakshi Amman
kanchipuram_kamakshi.architecture: Four named gopurams mark the restored enclosure. The HUDCO plan and aerial survey show a large west tank and teppam pavilion, the golden-vimana temple block, and separate Vasantha, Shukrawara, Navaratri and Vahana Mandapams. The in-game compound follows these footprints and is rotated to match the aerial view.
kanchipuram_kamakshi.attributes: Sugarcane bow; lotus/parrot; pasha and ankusha. Published accounts vary on hand assignment.
kanchipuram_kamakshi.deity_notes: The seated four-armed study uses the posture and attributes documented by the Devasthanam. Shri Chakra has its own place before the image.
kanchipuram_kamakshi.uncertainties: Detailed interior wall dimensions and subsidiary altar positions remain approximate. Some forms are based on written iconography and the associated ritual, since close views of the installed images remain unverified.

pradyumna_shrinkhala.architecture: Present-day Pandua Minar and roofless Bari Masjid, based on ASI photographs and a published site plan. The precise ancient Shrinkhala shrine remains unresolved. The model dimensions, spacing and damage are approximate.
pradyumna_shrinkhala.deity_form: No verified surviving original Shrinkhala image is supplied.
pradyumna_shrinkhala.deity_notes: No verified surviving original murti established. Do not present modern devotional artwork as a documented ancient original.
pradyumna_shrinkhala.uncertainties: The traditional Pradyumna/Pandua association does not authenticate the minaret as temple fabric. No daily worship or exact ancient temple footprint is asserted. Reused carvings and any inscriptions require object-level documentation.

mysore_chamundeshwari.name: Chamundeshwari
mysore_chamundeshwari.architecture: A long east–west quadrangle on Chamundi Hill. The seven-tiered eastern gopura leads through the entrance and Navaranga to the Antarala and west sanctum. The western vimana is smaller than the gateway tower. Aerial footprints and the temple authority’s sequence informed the model.
mysore_chamundeshwari.deity_form: Chamundeshwari as Mahishasuramardini, dressed in layered floral and metal adornment in the temple gallery.
mysore_chamundeshwari.arms: The game maintains eight in its sculptural study. Gallery adornment obscures the full arrangement.
mysore_chamundeshwari.attributes: Crown, flower garlands and ornamental arch as shown in the temple gallery.
mysore_chamundeshwari.deity_notes: The temple authority gallery shows several ceremonial and decorated forms. The game uses its floral adornment as a visual source.
mysore_chamundeshwari.uncertainties: Aerial imagery fixes the orientation and relative building footprints. Detailed interior dimensions, guardian sides, the original installed anatomy beneath adornment and some relief identities remain approximate.

alampur_jogulamba.name: Jogulamba
alampur_jogulamba.architecture: Present Jogulamba is a rebuilt shrine (2005), with a sculpted gateway and its own compound. Nearby ancient Navabrahma Shiva temples exhibit Badami Chalukyan forms; they are not interchangeable with the modern Devi temple.

alampur_jogulamba.attributes: Tongue extended; scorpion, frog and lizard on the head, as described by district government
alampur_jogulamba.deity_notes: Do not substitute a peaceful generic seated Devi or add a lion throne. Do not replace the district source's frog with a skull merely because another account differs.
alampur_jogulamba.uncertainties: Arm count, hand attributes and exact current ornaments remain unverified.

srisailam_bhramaramba.name: Bhramaramba–Mallikarjuna
srisailam_bhramaramba.architecture: The satellite footprint defines the four gated prakara and north and south perimeter ranges. Mallikarjuna stands on the eastern arrival axis beyond Nandi and Veerasiro. The elevated Bhramaramba terrace occupies the west end. Subsidiary shrines and covered wells follow relative locations described in the architectural record.
srisailam_bhramaramba.deity_form: Bhramaramba alankara and Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga, with separate sacred images and stops.
srisailam_bhramaramba.posture: Standing-style outline of the photographed dressed Bhramaramba. Mallikarjuna is worshipped as a lingam.
srisailam_bhramaramba.arms: The Bhramaramba kavacha and garlands conceal the underlying stone form in the model.
srisailam_bhramaramba.attributes: Gold kavacha, tiered crown, garlands and trishula study based on published darshan imagery. The Jyotirlinga has the historic serpent hood and suspended abhisheka vessel.
srisailam_bhramaramba.deity_notes: The alankara is modeled as seen in the published frontal image. Both principal darshan areas are treated as separate sacred spaces.
srisailam_bhramaramba.uncertainties: The major enclosure and roof positions are aerial references. Small-shrine bay positions and order, exact installed iconography, current visitor restrictions and some gateway dimensions remain approximate.

kolhapur_mahalakshmi.name: Mahalakshmi / Ambabai
kolhapur_mahalakshmi.architecture: Dark Deccan stone core with offset mouldings, connected mandapas and later lighter shikharas. Western Mahadwara leads through Garuda mandapa toward three west-facing sanctuaries.
kolhapur_mahalakshmi.attributes: Deity's lower right: citron; upper right: mace with head down; upper left: shield; lower left: bowl
kolhapur_mahalakshmi.deity_notes: Keep right/left relative to the deity, not the viewer. Do not replace these with four lotuses or generic blessing hands.
kolhapur_mahalakshmi.uncertainties: Ornaments and sari vary; the precise underlying sculpture and crown details need photographic comparison.

mahur_renuka.name: Ekaveerika / Renuka
mahur_renuka.architecture: Hilltop temple with a sanctum and assembly hall, a silver-clad doorway and a large worshipped face/head form. Steps and the hill approach are part of its setting.
mahur_renuka.posture: Face/head form, not a full standing body
mahur_renuka.arms: Not applicable to the visible main sacred form
mahur_renuka.attributes: Prominent painted eyes, facial ornaments and crown
mahur_renuka.deity_notes: Do not invent a full multi-armed body beneath the worshipped face. Preserve this temple's distinctive facial proportions.
mahur_renuka.uncertainties: Paint, jewellery and alankara change; distinguish decoration from the underlying form.

ujjain_mahakali.name: Mahakali / Harsiddhi
ujjain_mahakali.architecture: Maratha-period temple ensemble with two prominent lamp pillars before the shrine. The principal group comprises Annapurna between Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati; a Sri Yantra and old well are documented.
ujjain_mahakali.posture: Central Annapurna between Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati
ujjain_mahakali.attributes: Dark vermilion treatment and Sri Yantra are documented
ujjain_mahakali.deity_notes: Do not replace the three-image group with one generic four-armed Mahakali or borrow the nearby Gadkalika image.
ujjain_mahakali.uncertainties: Exact shape, scale and attributes of all three images need a verified frontal image.

pithapuram_puruhutika.name: Puruhutika / Padagaya
pithapuram_puruhutika.architecture: Puruhutika occupies the Kukkuteswara shared temple campus. Gateways, Shiva sanctum, Nandi, associated shrines and Padagaya water body determine the layout; it is not a freestanding Devi-only compound.
pithapuram_puruhutika.attributes: Seed bag (beeja), axe (parashu), lotus (kamala), dish (madhu patra); lower-right to lower-left order given in course
pithapuram_puruhutika.deity_notes: Do not use random weapons or confuse Puruhutika with Rajarajeshwari or a Dattatreya image from the shared campus.
pithapuram_puruhutika.uncertainties: Hand-order wording must be resolved visually before sculpting; do not mirror the image.

jajpur_biraja.architecture: Kalinga ensemble with rekha vimana, pidha jagamohana, front chandi mandapa and lion gate. The principal Biraja image is two-armed; Nabhigaya is a well within the enclosure.
jajpur_biraja.attributes: Right hand trident; left hand lifts the buffalo tail; left foot presses the demon
jajpur_biraja.deity_notes: Do not use the standard eight-/ten-armed lion-riding Durga template. The demon is buffalo-shaped.

draksharama_manikyamba.name: Manikyamba / Bhimeswara
draksharama_manikyamba.architecture: Eastern Chalukyan complex with two prakaras and four outer gateways. Two stairways access the upper sanctum around the tall Bhimeswara linga; Manikyamba occupies the northern inner gallery. The other named shrine groups occupy their documented eastern, southern and western galleries.

kamakhya.name: Kamarupa / Kamakhya
kamakhya.architecture: A west-facing sequence through the apsidal Natmandir, five-domed Bhogamandapa, Chalanta and Antarala to the eastern Vimana. IIT Guwahati figs. 33–36 inform hall footprints and door positions. The aerial view informs courtyard scale and roof silhouettes.
kamakhya.deity_form: Sacred natural rock and spring in the octagonal Manobhava Guha
kamakhya.posture: Three sacred stone forms share the lower chamber, 2.5 metres below the halls.
kamakhya.attributes: A spring-fed depression, natural stone, oil lamps and red offerings
kamakhya.deity_notes: Kamakhya/Sodasi, Matangi and Kamala have separate viewpoints in the shared cave. The movable Kameshwari and Kameshwara studies remain in Chalanta.
kamakhya.uncertainties: The cave contour and precise Matangi and Kamala positions are approximate. The two tanks are documented inside the precinct. Their exact game footprints, tree positions and remaining individual sculpture identities are estimates.

prayag_madhaveswari.name: Madhaveswari at Prayaga (game selects Alopi)
prayag_madhaveswari.architecture: The Alopibagh precinct has a rose bilingual street arch, a covered approach, a lion-flanked inner facade and a tall panelled shikhara over flat-roofed ranges. The nearby Lalita Devi temple at Mirapur is a separate identification and site.
prayag_madhaveswari.deity_notes: The covered cradle represents Alopi Shankari. The 2026 sanctum photograph shows four corner posts, silver relief panels, flowers and folded brocade over the kund. The district also documents a Shiva murti and a distinct Shiva lingam.
prayag_madhaveswari.uncertainties: The north-up aerial image establishes the visible roof masses and streets. Gate alignment and interior spacing remain approximations. A surveyed plan and photographs locating the individual Shiva forms were unavailable.

jwalamukhi_vaishnavi.name: Vaishnavi / Jwalamukhi
jwalamukhi_vaishnavi.architecture: Hillside temple complex with a gilded dome. Natural flames in rock fissures are worshipped as the central manifestation. Nine named flames share the sacred precinct.
jwalamukhi_vaishnavi.attributes: Nine named flame identities; actual visible flames may vary
jwalamukhi_vaishnavi.deity_notes: Do not replace the flames with one large idol or nine detached statues. Reject photos from Shaktinagar or Khrew.
jwalamukhi_vaishnavi.uncertainties: No authenticated close-up flame photograph selected; exact fissure positions remain unverified. Courtyard and dome silhouettes use published photo references; no measured plan or stone-by-stone reconstruction is claimed.

gaya_mangalagauri.name: Mangala Gauri
gaya_mangalagauri.architecture: Mangala Gauri is a small east-facing shrine atop Bhasmakut. The present exterior has low twin hipped roof forms dressed in cloth, marble-faced doorway panels and a checkered court edged by a modern canopy. A climb from the road links the hilltop to the city.

gaya_mangalagauri.posture: Sacred symbol, not established as a full anthropomorphic figure
gaya_mangalagauri.arms: Not applicable to the documented symbolic form
gaya_mangalagauri.attributes: Reliefs and ritual adornment belong to the setting
gaya_mangalagauri.deity_notes: Do not invent a large multi-armed main idol from a generic devotional poster.
gaya_mangalagauri.uncertainties: Exact terrain profiles, step dimensions, temple-internal carvings and the subsidiary bay sequence require more detailed documentation.

kashi_vishalakshi.name: Vishalakshi
kashi_vishalakshi.architecture: A compact south-influenced gateway inserted into the narrow residential lanes of Mir Ghat. Yellow plaster encloses a checkerboard entrance, a small mandapa, the two-image sanctum and a pradakshina route with Shiva and Nandi stops in three directions.
kashi_vishalakshi.deity_form: Dressed Vishalakshi darshan and the smaller Adi Vishalakshi image in the same sanctum
kashi_vishalakshi.posture: The larger clothed front form is documented in the field survey. Accounts place the smaller older form to the rear left.
kashi_vishalakshi.arms: Concealed by textiles in the photographed darshan
kashi_vishalakshi.attributes: Wide painted eyes, red garments, white and red garlands and a silver repousse canopy
kashi_vishalakshi.deity_notes: The main form follows the visible festival adornment in the VKM survey. The smaller image is represented by a devotional study of the reported second image.
kashi_vishalakshi.uncertainties: Aerial imagery shows the tight residential block. Exact frontage bearing, room dimensions, individual subsidiary bays and installed iconography still need measured confirmation.

kashmir_sharada.name: Saraswati / Sharada Peeth
kashmir_sharada.architecture: The Neelum Valley ruins are represented with the 35 × 26 m field-survey enclosure, 63-step western approach, damaged double porch, southern break, eastern postern and raised roofless sanctuary. The square sanctuary has a 3.8 m interior and opens west. The north wall retains a recessed chamber described in the archaeological record.

kashmir_sharada.attributes: Generic veena-bearing Saraswati imagery is not proof of this site's original sculpture
kashmir_sharada.deity_notes: The historic Sharada image is unverified. The separately consecrated Teetwal image belongs to the modern temple in Kupwara.
kashmir_sharada.uncertainties: The project uses the detailed field plan for orientation and dimensions. The Department of Archaeology and Museums entry describes the main entrance as north; the field plan places it west. Individual stone profiles, wall collapse, valley terrain and trefoil carving depth are approximate.
